walkthroughs.body_html:
Investigating Small Business — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Investigating Small Business brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Investigating Small Business.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Strategic
Specific
Strong
Saleable

mcqs.q: Which 1970 essay argued the 'social responsibility of business is to increase profits'?
options: Drucker
Porter
Friedman
Carroll

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.

mcqs.q: When might an autocratic leadership style be appropriate?
options: Autocratic leadership is always wrong and democratic leadership is always right.
In crises requiring quick decisions, when workers are inexperienced, or in highly hierarchical contexts — though it can damage morale long-term.
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
The level of output where total revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss. It is NOT the level where profit is maximised; profit grows beyond break-even.
Break-even is where the business makes the most profit.
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
